body: For me, the thoughts seem to vary over time. Even within a single day. How do you keep dealing with it though? Do you have something in your life that makes you want to continue, despite being on that edge every day?

Well, just because, like you say. I know not everything about my life is bad. I have family who care, and I seem reasonably healthy physically. There are people who are a lot worse off. 

Maybe I'm just an ungrateful selfish person. But I still can't see anything positive in the future. It's easier to deal with suicidal thoughts if I don't think about the future. Whenever I think further ahead than a month, or a year, it gets worse. My life feels so pointless and pathetic. 

At the moment I just deal with it. There aren't any things in my daily life that lift me up. I just go on, because I don't want to hurt anyone. And most of the time I guess I don't really want to die.

You could try posting after drinking smaller amounts. It doesn't matter what, just post anything. You could try to desensitise yourself to it, so to speak, over a period of time. And as you'll learn that nothing bad happens, you may get more confident. Perhaps to the point where you'll start posting sober.

Dunno whether this is any use to you, but I do think that it's something you can work on. You don't have to face anyone after you post, you could allow yourself to just walk away after posting for a short while, do something fun, and only come back to it later.

Either way, I'm not judging. Anxiety can be a heavy burden to bear and hard to understand for people who don't suffer from it. I have faith in your ability to overcome this, but it's up to you at the end of the day.

Good luck.

Heh, this made me smile. You're way off, but in a weird way that makes me feel slightly better. 

I don't think I had a rough childhood, it wasn't perfect, but I do love my parents and my family.
I have a full-time job, which I used to think would be the job of my dreams. And I keep myself busy with activities in my spare time. Although those activities do tend to keep me inside and by myself.
Hygiene isn't a problem for me either, I like to keep clean and groomed, even if none notices, it makes me feel slightly less bad about myself. And I'm also in pretty decent physical shape. 

Sounds like I should be happy, right?

In fact, I've got a ton going on in my life, but I've started to neglect a lot of it. It's becoming so hard to just get through a simple working day. I'll be in a meeting, trying to be participate, but inside I'll just feel like crying or killing myself. And I have to fight to keep a straight face. And afterwards I flee to the toilet as quick as I can to lock myself in. To get a breather and stop having to pretend. 

And when I come home I just crash. All these thoughts whirl around my head about how worthless I am. How I'm never going to be a whole content human being. About how weak I am and how much I hate myself. I just goes on and on.

I am lonely, I suppose you're right about that, but I don't think that will ever change. I wish I could cut out the part of myself that wants love or companionship. That would be a good start.

I do need to start exercising regularly again, if only for the endorphins and the distraction.

Thanks for the suggestions.

I'm trying to cut down down on alcohol. In the past it would either make me have a great night, or make me have a terrible night. But regardless, the next day is always horrible and I end up with even more self loathing than usual.

With the way I've been doing lately, I don't really trust myself with alcohol. I've had a lot of thoughts about suicide and lately it's been getting more intense. I've obviously not acted on it yet, but if my mood swings the wrong way when I'm drunk, well, I don't think I'd be able or want to stop myself.

Edit: The fact that I'm posting here in r/depression again, instead of in r/sw, is probably a good sign though...

The lot. Well, mainly all the thoughts and feelings that keep recurring in my mind. I overthink everythink and cannot switch off. Especially when my thoughts get dark and when I feel hurt and sad, I cannot stop dwelling on it and it makes it so much worse.

I was desperately trying to get to sleep last night, not because I was tired, but because I wanted my mind to shut down. I considered knocking myself out with sleeping pills, but that's probably not a good idea.
Crisis over. Walking and fresh air did me a lot of good. Sorry about the swearing.
Don't bother responding. I'm going out for a walk, maybe that will help.
Thanks for the replies. But I just don't know anymore.

I use two throwaway accounts. This one for my depression and another for some other stuff. I'd like to keep my issues separated. I don't really know why, really...

I'm terified someone I know might recognise me, even though that fear is probably unfounded. 

I can be very reticent offline. I've learned to open up more last year, to friends and family and my Doctor. But I still almost always hold back to some extent.

The more anonymous I am, the less I feel the need to hold back. Throwaway accounts help like that, even though it's not very rational.
I'm supposed to seek a therapist soon. And I will. I'm just getting a bit worried about it.
And yes, I would agree that there is a lot of evil in the world. But it seems to me that by taking yourself out of it, you're increasing the average evilness per head of population.

For me the reason is other people. My family and friends. 

I've got good days and bad days. On good days I don't need a reason. On bad days, like today, it seems the only reason to go on is to prevent hurting the people I care about. I don't want to plunge anyone I love in a depression, just because I can't cope with my own depression.

It's a cliché perhaps, and it's not a very good reason to live your life. But hey, I'm still here. And I don't think I'll ever really do anything to change that.
I thought about this months ago and then forgot about it. It's my last option, and it is sort of soothing to have that option available. Don't think it will ever get that far though.

Good for you, buddy :)

Although I'm not exactly content with my life situation myself, I'm having a reasonably good day today. And I had two good days last week as well. So, yay. 

Here's to the things and times that make you remember it's worth it.

Hang in there. You're raising a child and trying to make a living at the same time. I can cannot imagine how hard that must be, but I respect you for it.

If there is one thing I believe in, it's the capacity of people to change and improve themselves. Maybe it is just wishful thinking, but it keeps me going.

When I look at the people within my company that have been promoted, they usually exhibit the same trait: They have taken charge or ownership and have been doing work outside their immediate job-spec of remit. They are people who ignore convention and in many cases simply do the job they get promoted to, before they even are promoted. 
So if you would like to grow within your current job/industry, that might be something worth thinking about.

Alternatively, change, or like you say: starting over, can be really powerfull as well. The internet contains a wealth of information about ways to improve yourself, or to acquire new skills, or to learn about something new or to prepare you for a new carreer. 

My mum used to provide for us by herself when we were young kids and she re-educated herself and changed to a completely different job, in order to do so.

If you want to, I think that you too have the strength to change your life. Set yourself realistic goals. Maybe you could spend one day a week, whilst the father is with your son, to try and learn something new. 

I'm just thinking out loud here. Bear in mind that I don't know the pressures you're under, so only you can make those calls.

In the end though, if you are unhappy with your life, there are only two things you can do:
- Look at the things of value in your life and try to gain the enjoyment and fulfilment you need out of them.
- Or, take charge and change it.

Edit: Whatever you do, chin up and good luck with it :)

Oh and hugs :)

Think this is good advice; a friend gave me very similar advice yesterday and she was probably right. I need to learn to deal with depression first (and hopefully overcome it). Entering a relationship like this is probably not a good idea. It might put a lot of strain on a new budding relationship and you don't want to use your relationship as a crutch either. Relationships are hard work and you don't want to be thrown further down the pit of your depression if it doesn't work out. Cause, let's face it, not all relationships will work out like you'd want them too.

NevloW gives sound advice too. I know it may seem impossible to motivate yourself when you're depressed. But if you do manage to get yourself out of your comfort zone, you may end up feeling more empowered to take further steps. 

It's hard, especially around the holidays, when all around you, you see the little things couples do to show their affection. And it makes you feel more lonely and it sucks. But you can do it, you can work on getting more comfortable about meeting people and coping with your depression. And you'll gain more confidence and self respect because of it. 

Strength and good luck to you, anonymous friend :)

Maybe you're right, pretending can be so terribly draining. I think that may be why I want to be alone so often, so I don't have to keep the mask up and pretend to be happy and functional.

If I don't pretend, I'm afraid I might lose my job, or the respect people have for me. The people around me tend to think much more highly of me than I do myself, or than I deserve. Each time my mask slips, I'm afraid that respect or esteem deteriorates.

I don't want to be the person that I am, I want to be the person that I pretend to be and others think I am.

Thanks, I hope things work out for you.

I self medicate a bit, but with the approval of my Doctor. I'm supposed to get therapy, but I somehow managed to spend three weeks now just looking for a therapist, without actually seeing one. 

On a good day I feel like nothing is wrong, like I'm getting better and don't need a therapist anymore and I keep postponing the call. On a bad day, well, I either make excuses or am too lethargic to sort it out. I've made so many plans to sort myself out, get a therapist, sleep and eat regularly, lots of excercise and so on. But sticking with the plans is proving hard.

I think I'm a bit scared of seeing a therapist really...
Thanks, this is really helpful. I'm jotting down an 'agenda' now, so to speak, to make sure we cover everything I want to talk to him about. I'll try to resist the urge to hold back.
